record.title: EMP Protection and Resilience Guidelines v2.2 (2019)
record.locator: Printed34-35,55 and Appendix A; historical 2019 guidance, not current product certification
record.finding: Risk depends on exposure/coupling. The guide supports disconnecting spare equipment, overlapping heavy-duty foil and checking penetrations. It cautions that unmodified trash cans are unreliable and small disconnected handheld electronics are relatively immune. Frequency-specific engineering acceptance testing is separate from a phone reception check.

record.title: Solar Storms and Flares
record.finding: Earth-directed solar storms can disrupt infrastructure; Earth’s magnetic field and atmosphere protect people at the surface. The book’s analogy to losing Earth’s atmosphere like Mars is not an established present disaster scenario.

record.title: Keeping the Lights On in North America
record.finding: Changing magnetic fields induce geoelectric fields and currents in long power-grid lines. Regional geology affects exposure; transformer damage and prolonged outages are possible, not a prediction that every device fails.

record.title: Medical Devices and Natural Disasters
record.locator: General Safety and Power Outage; bleach instructions on this older multi-topic page are not adopted
record.finding: Plan compatible battery/generator power with manufacturer instructions, check device settings after restoration and obtain help for life-sustaining equipment. Do not store an actively required device away instead of providing needed therapy.

record.title: Home Water Treatment Systems
record.finding: Testing and contaminant-specific treatment are required. Filter pore size and certification matter; charcoal appearance/adsorption alone does not establish removal of pathogens or chemicals.

record.title: Collecting Rainwater and Your Health
record.finding: Rainwater can acquire germs and chemicals before or after collection. Intended use, testing, treatment, maintenance and separation from potable pipes matter.

record.title: Guidelines for Testing Well Water
record.finding: Use a state-certified laboratory, annual indicators and locally relevant/event-driven tests. A clear well or a household filter is not a potability finding.

record.title: 12VAC5-630-410: Well construction
record.finding: Geology, siting, casing, sanitary construction and well class matter. Class IV construction protects groundwater but does not ensure potable supply. The outline does not establish an approved DIY drinking-water well.

record.title: How to Create an Emergency Water Supply
record.finding: Store at least one gallon per person daily for three days and aim for two weeks; add needs for conditions and uses. Containers, sanitation, dates and rotation matter. This is not an unlimited water availability or garden-demand estimate.

record.title: Composting at Home
record.finding: Backyard composting needs appropriate browns/greens, moisture and aeration; ordinary piles should avoid fish/meat/bones. Compost recycles nutrients; it does not create nitrogen from nothing. Beer/ammonia additives are not validated by this guide.

record.title: Use of Manure and Other Soil Amendments of Animal Origin
record.finding: Raw animal manure needs pathogen, incorporation, harvest-interval and runoff controls. Merely aged manure is still raw if not properly composted; rabbit droppings are not exempt on the basis that they do not burn plants.

record.title: Nongame Fishing Regulations
record.locator: Methods to Capture or Take; requirements reviewed November2,2026
record.finding: Public-water juglines must remain within sight, with species, waters, labeling and numerical restrictions. Nets/traps and spearing have separate restrictions; an outage does not automatically suspend fishing rules.

record.title: Keep Food Safe After an Emergency
record.finding: Use appliance thermometers and time/temperature history during outages; refrigeration loss does not instantly make all food unsafe. No smell or improvised preservation method substitutes for temperature controls.

record.title: Ensuring Safe Canned Foods
record.finding: Use tested food-specific canning processes, including pressure processing for low-acid foods. Cultural attribution or a sealed sanitized jar is not sufficient validation.

record.title: Sun Drying
record.finding: Outdoor drying is inappropriate for meat and most vegetables under uncontrolled conditions. Fruit drying depends on suitable heat, humidity, air movement and protection.

record.title: Seasonal Allergies and Complementary Health Approaches
record.finding: There is no convincing evidence that honey relieves seasonal allergies. This finding does not establish the book’s other wound, hair or throat uses.

record.title: Carbon Monoxide Poisoning Basics
record.finding: Fuel-burning devices can produce fatal CO. Keep portable generators outside away from openings, never use charcoal or camp stoves indoors, and maintain alarms/approved venting.

record.title: Linseed Oil
record.finding: Linseed oil can self-heat in oily rags and ignite nearby combustibles if heat accumulates. Tool-oiling plans need product-label handling and waste controls.

record.title: Food Storage Conditions
record.finding: Moisture uptake and heat degrade dry-food storage. Packaging and product-specific processing matter; this does not establish a twenty-year life for every freeze-dried recipe.

record.title: Getting the Most Out of Food Storage
record.finding: Moist food in reduced-oxygen packaging can create botulism risk. The source describes about 10% or less moisture for airtight oxygen-absorber storage, not a visual dryness test.

record.title: EMP scope and certainty
record.guidance: Separate nuclear E1/E2/E3 effects, localized intentional interference and solar geomagnetic disturbance. Exposure, conductor geometry and equipment response vary. Neither all devices fail nor all old vehicles survive is established. Preserve the book’s early caveats and later contradictions.

record.title: Shielding performance
record.guidance: Conductivity, seams, penetrations, frequency and field strength matter. Tight-looking lids, plastic inner boxes and ordinary metal tape do not establish quantified shielding. Electrical insulation can prevent shorts/contact hazards; a plastic box is not another conductive shield. No specific DIY build is certified.

record.title: Reception tests
record.guidance: A ringing phone can reveal leakage at that service band; a silent phone is not a broadband EMP acceptance test. Preserve the source’s explicit limitation and later Wi-Fi-test warning. No attenuation, waveform or pass threshold is measured.

record.title: Electrical installation and restoration
record.guidance: Use qualified assessment and the actual equipment instructions for bonding, surge protection, transfer equipment and isolation. Do not remove protective grounding or make live panel/solar repairs from this outline. The generic controller-before-battery sequence is not universally safe.

record.title: Medical priorities
record.guidance: Keep essential therapy available. Plan compatible power, consumables, duration and escalation with care team/manufacturer; store suitable spares rather than disconnect an actively needed life-support device.

record.title: Radio capability and costs
record.guidance: Match receiving bands, range, power, antennas, training and applicable operating authorization to a communication plan. A radio or container does not guarantee broadcasts or two-way service. The $200/$50 prices are not current quotations; no product endorsement or license waiver inferred.

record.title: Water source and treatment
record.guidance: Stored safe water, source assessment and contaminant-matched treatment are separate tasks. Rainwater is not automatically potable; loose charcoal/sand/grass and boiling do not establish universal chemical/pathogen removal. Do not treat this sketch as a drinking-water filter specification.

record.title: Well and water budgets
record.guidance: Do not assume drilling is simple, necessary, lawful or yields enough. Evaluate geology, approved construction, quality, pump access/power and measured sustainable yield. The irrigation well is not assigned potable or outage capacity.

record.title: Fire and fuel use
record.guidance: Use suitable equipment, ventilation, clearances, fuel handling and actual local fire restrictions. The fire triangle needs heat, fuel and oxygen, not specifically a spark. Outdoor fire skills do not authorize indoor combustion.

record.title: Shelter and security
record.guidance: Prioritize safe evacuation/alternative lodging, lawful assistance, de-escalation and safe exits. Do not turn armed harassment or retaking territory into household tasks. Door barricades/weights can obstruct egress or injure people; bunker ventilation, drainage and structural design are unassessed.

record.title: Fishing feasibility and rules
record.guidance: Do not rely on guaranteed catch or lifetime gear. Confirm water/species/method/size/consumption rules. Virginia public-water juglines require attendance within sight; the proposed leave-all-day use is not approved.

record.title: Food preparation and cold chain
record.guidance: Use tested recipes and temperature/handling controls. The dough’s salt line is ambiguous, actual incorporated flour is variable, and no baking temperature/time is supplied. No scratch-cooking method is automatically nutritionally complete or safe.

record.title: Garden claims and inputs
record.guidance: Assess sun, soil, crop variety, irrigation, nutrient rates and pests. Companion pairs and seed-saving permanence are not established guarantees. A well or creek does not supply unlimited suitable crop water; tap-water chlorine is not shown here to destroy all soil microbiology.

record.title: Compost and fertilizers
record.guidance: Use suitable inputs, air and moisture. Do not adopt fish/muck ratios or beer/ammonia spraying as validated backyard compost recipes; natural overfeeding can also harm soil/water. Nutrients are recycled, not created by decomposition.

record.title: Tools and repair
record.guidance: Match tools and maintenance to manufacturer instructions and skills, with safe sharpening and oily-rag handling. Electronics should not be categorically excluded from repair planning because of an assumed total failure.

record.title: Preservation process
record.guidance: Follow tested food-specific canning, curing, smoking or drying controls. Mold trimming is not a universal salvage rule for arbitrary meat. A specialty properly cured country ham is not interchangeable with other hams or dried sausage. No full recipe in this chapter is approved.

record.title: Freeze-drying and oxygen absorbers
record.guidance: The twenty-year claim is explicitly about freeze-drying, not all sun-dried food. Product, processing endpoint, packaging, residual moisture, temperature and stability data remain necessary; no universal shelf life adopted.

record.title: Livestock constraints
record.guidance: Confirm lawful keeping, species-specific feed, water, health, reproduction, welfare and processing. Do not assume disaster cancels local rules, that goats lactate continuously without a breeding cycle or that hens eradicate all ticks. Raw rabbit manure needs food-crop controls.

record.title: Honey health uses
record.guidance: Honey is not an established seasonal-allergy treatment. Household honey is not interchangeable with a clinician-selected sterile wound product. No dose, wound indication or safe formulation is approved here.

record.title: Bee management
record.guidance: Use local competent husbandry, siting, protective equipment, allergy planning, pest monitoring and fire-safe smoker handling. Water/fence/smoke alone is not a complete system; honey, pollination and subsidy claims are not guaranteed.

record.title: Permaculture and yield
record.guidance: The narrative says six plant types but lists seven. Preserve all seven, and treat concentric layout, rain-only water and camouflage as research concepts rather than definitions, safety guarantees or demonstrated food sufficiency.

An Army Engineer’s Emp-Proof Home Guide 
15 
4. Water System Components 
You can survive weeks without food under the right conditions, but water is a much 
shorter clock, and many homes rely on electrically powered systems to access it without 
their owners fully realizing it.  
A well that has no functioning pump controller is just a hole in the ground, and a filtration 
system with dead electronics is just an expensive piece of hardware sitting uselessly in 
your garage. 
The components worth prioritizing here include: 
• well pump controllers 
• electronic pump components 
• water filtration systems with electronic parts 
• UV purification devices 
If these components fail and you have no backup, your access to clean water can 
disappear overnight even if the physical infrastructure around you is perfectly intact.  
Water is the foundation of short-term survival, and protecting the systems that deliver it 
deserves to be treated with that level of seriousness. 
5. Vehicles 
This is the most misunderstood category in EMP preparation, partly because not all 
vehicles will fail and partly because people tend to think about the vehicle as a whole 
rather than the specific components that make it vulnerable.  
Losing your vehicle after an EMP means losing the ability to evacuate, run supply trips, 
relocate if needed, or maintain any kind of strategic mobility in a situation where flexibility 
is everything. 
The most practical approach involves thinking about: 
• older vehicles with simpler electronics, which have significantly better survival 
odds 
• spare electronic components like ECUs and ignition modules stored in a 
protected location 
• small electric transport options like e -bikes or scooters, if they are properly 
shieldedYou do not necessarily need to shield your entire vehicle, but having 
backup components stored safely can be the difference between being 
completely stuck and having options when everyone around you does not.

Why These Five 
The logic behind this list comes down to a simple framework that cuts through the noise 
of most EMP preparation advice. No communication leaves you without awareness. No 
backup power leaves you without capability.  
No medical devices creates an immediate and potentially fatal risk. No working water 
systems creates a survival problem within days. No transportation removes your 
flexibility at exactly the moment you need it most. 
Everything else is secondary to these five, and while that does not mean other 
preparations are worthless, it does mean that your time, resources, and protected 
storage space should flow to this list before anything else.  
If a device keeps you alive, keeps you informed, or keeps you capable of functioning and 
moving, it deserves protection. If it does not meet at least one of those criteria, it can 
wait. 
Most people will lose every electronic device they depend on in a single moment they 
never saw coming. By focusing your preparation on these five categories before anything 
else, you give yourself something that will be genuinely rare in that environment: a 
working advantage when it matters most.

Even a small gap can allow energy to leak inside, and even brief direct contact between a 
device and the metal shell can transfer enough energy to destroy it. A Faraday cage is only 
as strong as its weakest point, which means every detail in the construction matters. 
The 3-Layer System 
The most reliable way to protect your electronics is to use a layered approach rather than 
relying on a single barrier. Three layers of protection working together reduce the chance 
of failure far more than any single well-built container could on its own. 
Layer 1: The Outer Conductive Shield 
This is your primary defense, and it needs to be fully conductive, completely continuous, 
and enclosed on all sides with no exceptions. Good options for the outer shell include: 
• a metal trash can with a tight-fitting lid 
• an ammo can with proper sealing 
• a metal filing cabinet 
• a steel toolbox 
The quality of the seal determines the quality of the protection, and the lid deserves 
particular attention because it is where most failures occur. You want tight contact 
between the lid and the body of the container, with no visible gaps anywhere along t he 
seam.  
Aluminum conductive tape applied around the lid edge is not required, but it 
meaningfully improves the seal and is worth using if you want to take the protection 
seriously. 
Layer 2: The Insulation Barrier 
This is the layer most people skip entirely, which is a significant mistake because it is one 
of the most important parts of the system.  
The purpose of this layer is to prevent your electronics from making any contact with the 
conductive outer shell, because if they touch it, the energy collected by that shell can 
transfer directly into the device and destroy it.  
To insulate properly, line the entire interior of your container completely using any of the 
following: 
• cardboard 
• foam padding

Every surface needs to be covered, including the bottom, all sides, and the inside of the 
lid, leaving no exposed metal anywhere that a device could potentially touch.

The third layer adds redundancy inside the main container, giving your devices a backup 
level of protection in case anything gets through the first two. This inner layer does not 
need to be metal. Small boxes, plastic containers, or individually wrapped bu ndles all 
work well.  
For higher levels of protection, you can wrap devices in foil after insulating them first, or 
place them inside smaller metal containers nested within the main one. Think of this 
layer as a secondary shield that exists specifically for the scenarios where the first layer 
alone might not be enough.

You do not need expensive or specialized equipment to put this together, and a basic 
version that provides solid protection can be built with materials that are easy to find and 
affordable. 
Step 1: Get a metal container with a lid. A galvanized steel trash can is one of the most 
practical and widely available options, though an ammo can or steel toolbox works just 
as well if you have one available. 
Step 2: Line the entire interior. Use cardboard or foam to cover every internal surface, 
including the bottom, all sides, and the inside of the lid, making sure absolutely no 
exposed metal remains anywhere that a device could come into contact with.

cloth, paper, or plastic first, and then add a layer of foil around the outside of that 
wrapping if you want an additional level of protection on each device.

and well cushioned so that nothing is pressing directly against the walls or shifting around 
inside.

That process is straightforward, repeatable, and effective when followed with care at

The Upgraded Version 
If you want to push the protection further, a more robust setup involves using an ammo 
can with an insulated lining as your outer container, wrapping each device individually 
with both an insulation layer and foil, placing those wrapped devices inside the sealed 
ammo can, and storing the entire container on a wood surface rather than directly on the 
ground.  
This approach creates multiple genuine layers of defense and meaningfully improves 
your odds compared to a single-container setup. 
What to Store Inside 
The priority list for what goes into your Faraday cage should mirror the priorities covered 
in the previous chapter, with the most critical items being: 
• ham radios and walkie-talkies 
• backup batteries 
• solar charge controllers and inverters 
• medical devices 
• USB drives containing important documents or information 
• small LED lights and other compact electronics 
If something is critical to your survival and it runs on electronics, it belongs inside the 
cage. 
Testing Your Faraday Cage 
You do not need laboratory equipment to get a reasonable sense of whether your setup 
is working. A simple test involves placing a phone inside the container, sealing the lid 
completely, and then calling that phone from another device. If the phone rings, signal is 
getting through and your cage has gaps that need to be addressed.  
If the phone receives no signal at all, your shielding is working at a level that should 
provide meaningful protection. This test is not a perfect measure of EMP protection 
specifically, but it is far better than simply hoping the construction is correct.

An Army Engineer’s Emp-Proof Home Guide 
30 
How to Protect Your Setup 
Store backup components. This is the most practical approach for most people. Rather 
than trying to shield your entire system, protect spare versions of the parts most likely to 
fail and swap them in if needed.  
For generators, store a spare ignition module and a backup voltage regulator. For solar 
systems, prioritize a spare charge controller and a backup inverter. Keep all of these 
inside a properly built Faraday cage, insulated, sealed, and clearly labeled. 
Keep systems disconnected when possible. EMP energy travels through connected 
systems, so the more connected your equipment is during an event, the more exposed it 
becomes.  
If you have any advance warning, disconnect generators from their loads and isolate solar 
components where it is safe to do so. 
Avoid unnecessary complexity. The more advanced and automated your power setup is, 
the more electronics it depends on and the more potential failure points it has.  
Simpler generators and basic solar configurations are more resilient, and manual backup 
options are worth building in wherever practical. 
Store a small backup power system. Keep a compact secondary setup inside a Faraday 
cage as a safety net.  
A small inverter, a compact charge controller, a foldable solar panel, and a battery pack 
stored together give you emergency lighting and enough power to run your 
communications equipment even if your primary system is completely lost. 
The Right Question to Ask 
Instead of asking whether your generator will survive an EMP , ask whether you have what 
you need to get it working again if it does not. Power after an EMP is not about having the 
largest system. It is about having a system that still works, or the means t o restore it 
quickly, while everyone around you is starting from nothing.

Chapter 7: Whole-House EMP Surge Protection: What 
Actually Helps and What Doesn't 
When people start thinking about protecting their homes from an EMP , one of the first 
things they look at is surge protection.  
We already use surge protectors for lightning and power spikes, so the assumption is that 
installing better versions of the same technology will provide meaningful coverage. That 
thinking is understandable, but it is only partially correct. 
The Difference Between Lightning and EMP 
Most surge protection devices are designed for lightning strikes and standard power 
surges, which are relatively slow and predictable. An EMP is a different problem entirely. 
It is faster, operates at higher frequencies, and can affect systems before conventional 
protection hardware has time to react. Some surge protectors will not respond quickly 
enough, and others may be overwhelmed entirely by the scale of energy involved. 
What Surge Protection Can and Cannot Do 
Surge protection needs to be understood for what it actually is: damage reduction rather 
than damage prevention. It can reduce the impact of secondary surges, help protect 
against grid instability after an event, and add a useful layer to a broader preparation plan. 
What it cannot do is fully protect your home from the initial EMP pulse or guarantee the 
survival of sensitive electronics. 
The Layered Approach 
Rather than relying on any single solution, the right strategy is to think in layers. A practical 
setup looks like this: a whole-house surge protector installed at your electrical panel as 
a first line of defence, handling grid fluctuations and residual surges before they spread 
through your wiring point-of-use surge protectors on key appliances and electronics as a 
second layer, useful for smaller surges and residual energy after the main event 
Faraday cage protection for your most critical devices as the third and most reliable layer. 
Each layer handles what it can handle, and together they cover far more ground than any 
one of them could alone.

An Army Engineer’s Emp-Proof Home Guide

The Hard Truth 
There is no guaranteed way to fully EMP -proof an entire modern home. Your wiring acts 
as an antenna, your home is connected to long external lines, and the energy involved in 
a significant EMP exceeds the design limits of conventional protection hardware. The goal 
is not perfection. It is meaningful risk reduction combined with protected backups that 
give you something to work with after the event. 
The biggest practical impact in any preparation plan does not come from surge 
protection. It comes from unplugging devices when possible, storing critical electronics 
in Faraday cages, and keeping backup components ready to deploy. Surge protection 
supports that plan, but it does not replace the fundamentals. 
What to Avoid 
Relying on surge protection alone leaves you significantly exposed. Assuming that any 
system labelled military-grade or industrial -strength is immune to EMP damage is a 
misunderstanding of how the technology works.  
And overlooking backups on the assumption that your protection will hold is the kind of 
thinking that leaves people starting from nothing when it matters most. 
Combining solid surge protection with properly stored backups and Faraday -protected 
devices moves you from broadly vulnerable to genuinely prepared, and in a situation 
where most people lose everything at once, that difference is worth taking seriously.

When an EMP hits, the damage happens in an instant. But what you do in the hours that

One of the most common mistakes people will make is rushing, flipping switches, 
plugging things in, and trying to see what still works without any structure or caution. In

intentional, and sequential.

additional damage.

39 
are looking for whether it powers on normally, functions as expected, and shows no signs 
of damage such as unusual heat, smell, or erratic behaviour.  
If anything seems off, stop using it immediately and set it aside. Do not plug multiple 
devices in at once, do not connect anything to an unknown power source, and do not 
assume something is fine without testing it. 
Step 3: Bring Systems Back Online Gradually 
Once you know what is working, you can begin rebuilding your systems, starting small 
and adding load incrementally rather than connecting everything at once. 
If you are using a generator, start it with no load attached, let it stabilize, and then connect 
devices one at a time while monitoring the output. If you are using a solar setup, test the 
charge controller first, then the battery system, then the inverter , and only then begin 
connecting loads gradually.  
If the grid happens to still be active, approach reconnection with caution, use isolated 
circuits where possible, and be prepared for instability in the supply. 
The order in which you bring things back online matters, and the priority should follow the 
same logic as the rest of this book: 
• communication devices first, because awareness is your most immediate need 
• basic lighting next, for safety and basic productivity 
• water systems after that, because this is a short-term survival priority 
• power generation capability last, as the foundation for everything longer term 
Everything beyond those four categories can wait until the immediate situation is stable 
and understood. 
The Rule to Follow 
The process is straightforward and worth committing to regardless of how urgent things 
feel in the moment: test first, confirm it is working as expected, and only then connect it 
to anything else.  
Rushing that sequence is how people destroy functional equipment in the hours after an 
event, and it is entirely avoidable with a small amount of discipline and a clear plan 
prepared in advance.

4. Metal Trash Cans 
A galvanized steel trash can is one of the simplest and most effective ready -made 
Faraday cage options available. It offers a fully enclosed metal body, minimal setup 
requirements, and enough storage capacity for a meaningful collection of protected 
devices.  
Line the interior with insulation, store your wrapped devices inside, and seal the lid as 
tightly as possible, adding aluminium tape around the seam for additional coverage. 
5. Ammo Cans 
Ammo cans are the best option for smaller and more portable setups, particularly the 
communications kit described in Chapter 0.4. Their thick metal construction, tight -
sealing lids, and durability make them a compact and reliable choice for storing radios,  
batteries, and other small critical electronics.  
Line the interior with insulation before loading anything inside and  seal the lid with 
aluminium tape for a more complete barrier. 
6. Aluminum Tape 
Most Faraday cage failures happen at the seams, which is exactly the problem aluminium 
tape is designed to solve. It is conductive, flexible, and effective at sealing the gaps and 
joints that represent the weakest points in any metal container setup.  
Applied around lid seams and edges, it is a small addition that makes a meaningful 
difference to the overall integrity of your protection. 
How to Combine These Materials 
The real effectiveness comes from combining these materials into a coherent layered 
system rather than relying on any single one.  
A practical example that uses everything on this list would look like this: a steel trash can 
as the outer layer, cardboard or foam lining the entire interior, devices wrapped 
individually in cloth with an outer layer of aluminium foil, and aluminium tape sealing the

To the frontiersman or even the early settler building a fire was second nature. You must 
consider the flow of oxygen  when  building  your  fire.

whatever border material  you  use.  Also  allow  some  space  between your tinder and 
the smaller kindling. If you  are  concerned  about  airflow  while the fire is burning either 
rearrange the fuel or blow into the base of the fire. 
Tinder 
We have been talking about tinder a lot and if you are not familiar with this world I want 
you to consider the materials that catch fire easily and burn hot.  
To me, good tinder is all about being able to catch off a minimal spark and burn hot. Many 
people have seen the magnesium and ferro rod combos. 
These work well because the magnesium burns so hot. I like to use magnesium in

Chapter 14 - Water Collection 
Following an EMP the water pipes may not run dry right away. However, the danger in 
those pipes increases drastically. The problem with the water in the tap is that water 
treatment will cease.  
There will be no way for you to tell if the water has suffered from backflow contamination 
or other types of contamination. It will be crucial for you to begin collecting water ASAP . 
Of course, collection comes in two forms. There is collection of water prior to the attack 
and there is collection after the attack. Both systems will need to be put in place 
beforehand.  
Right now, we have nearly unlimited access to potable water. You can buy gallons and 
bottles for just a few dollars. Do not miss out on this moment in time. You will never be 
hurt by having more water around then you need. There is no downside. Storing by the 
gallon is the best method. 
You could also purchase things like water bricks in order to utilize the free tap water. 
These bricks get filled and stack well for later use. These storage methods take advantage 
of modern day tactics. You will need to look back through the ages to discover other ways 
to collect water. 
Rain water will become precious. You  will  find  that  your  ability  to  channel water off 
roofs or collect water in  buckets  will  be  the  most important  part  of this method of 
collection. The larger container you have to fill the more you will be a ble to store, 
naturally. One of the best  ways  to  do  this is  collecting  water from your slanted roof. 
However,  there  are  concerns  about  the  asphalt  roof tiles. 
Detached collection vessels can  collect  rain  directly  from  the  sky.  Some  days the rain 
will pour and some days it will be dry. Between stored water and your rainwater collection 
you may find that your  water  needs  are  met.  That  said, there are other options as well. 
Since 8000 BC we have been drilling wells. This is not a new concept. There are aquifers 
beneath the ground that carry gallons of water that could be used to hydrate your family 
and your garden as you become more self-sufficient after an EMP .  
The understanding of this hydro cycle by which the aquifers can be tapped goes all the

Chapter 14 - Water Collection 
Following an EMP the water pipes may not run dry right away. However, the danger in 
those pipes increases drastically. The problem with the water in the tap is that water 
treatment will cease.  
There will be no way for you to tell if the water has suffered from backflow contamination 
or other types of contamination. It will be crucial for you to begin collecting water ASAP . 
Of course, collection comes in two forms. There is collection of water prior to the attack 
and there is collection after the attack. Both systems will need to be put in place 
beforehand.  
Right now, we have nearly unlimited access to potable water. You can buy gallons and 
bottles for just a few dollars. Do not miss out on this moment in time. You will never be 
hurt by having more water around then you need. There is no downside. Storing by the 
gallon is the best method. 
You could also purchase things like water bricks in order to utilize the free tap water. 
These bricks get filled and stack well for later use. These storage methods take advantage 
of modern day tactics. You will need to look back through the ages to discover other ways 
to collect water. 
Rain water will become precious. You  will  find  that  your  ability  to  channel water off 
roofs or collect water in  buckets  will  be  the  most important  part  of this method of 
collection. The larger container you have to fill the more you will be a ble to store, 
naturally. One of the best  ways  to  do  this is  collecting  water from your slanted roof. 
However,  there  are  concerns  about  the  asphalt  roof tiles. 
Detached collection vessels can  collect  rain  directly  from  the  sky.  Some  days the rain 
will pour and some days it will be dry. Between stored water and your rainwater collection 
you may find that your  water  needs  are  met.  That  said, there are other options as well. 
Since 8000 BC we have been drilling wells. This is not a new concept. There are aquifers 
beneath the ground that carry gallons of water that could be used to hydrate your family 
and your garden as you become more self-sufficient after an EMP .  
The understanding of this hydro cycle by which the aquifers can be tapped goes all the 
way back to the 1500’s.

Drilling a well on your property will become an essential part of your survival. The process

drill a well themselves using these tools.

using a farm animal or  even  manpower  to  turn  a  powerful  drill would be an option after 
the devastating effects of an EMP . If it worked on the ground in the 19th century it will still 
work today. 
Filtering 
Despite having access to this new source of well water you may still be at risk. You will 
not be able to send your well water off to be tested so how will you know if it is safe to 
drink as is? The answer is you won't.  
By simply drinking the water from the new well without testing you are putting your family 
at risk. Get yourself a high-quality filter for the home and one for the road as well. In other 
words, something that travels well. 
Store some high quality activated charcoal as well. By having  this  stuff  on hand, you can 
create your own filters for water that will then be boiled. I like the activated charcoal 
because it is the most absorbent and has the  most surface area for catching debris and 
pathogens.

An Army Engineer’s Emp-Proof Home Guide 
52 
Chapter 15 - Securing Shelter 
You might be considering why someone would be  worried  about  a  shelter  if  they have 
a home. There are  some  very important  things  to consider  following an EMP and one is 
that your home could be taken.  
Your home could be taken by a marauding force of desperate people  or  it  could  be  taken  
by  a  military force that has decided it's a good strategic point. 
There are many steps you can take to provide yourself shelter if yours has been 
compromised. Each method will take some  preparation  but  I  like  to  break shelter into 
three distinct types: 
• Building Shelter 
• Hidden Prefab Shelter 
• Taking Shelter Back 
When you remove the security of your own home there is a lot of inherent risk. Things like 
the elements, wildlife, human threats and actual death become very real when you are 
securing a new shelter. Your location is crucial when considering your strategy as well. 
Building a Shelter 
Whether we are talking about building shelter from tarps and tents or building shelter 
using bushcraft skills that are comprised of only the forest around you are building 
shelter.

An Army Engineer’s Emp-Proof Home Guide 
53 
Investing in  a  quality  tent  or  even  a  few  single  person tents that carry well are great 
ways to assure you have a dependable shelter in times of need.  
With the explosion in the outdoor adventure industry the market for quality tents has 
widened. There are so many great companies out there that are creating quality products. 
You can do a lot with your tent besides survive an EMP blast and the horrors that  will 
follow. 
Still, there is something to be said about building a simple lean to and learning how to live 
out in the woods. Most structures that you build out of sticks, cordage and leaves will not 
be the best for long term living but if you add a  simple tarp to these structures you will 
create much better shelter that can face the elements. 
The pioneers and the Native Americans were some of the best campers in American 
history. I like to look to them for an understanding of how shelter should be handled.  
They are my source for best practices, if you will. You did not see pioneers saddle up 
under a lean to or a shelter that was built of tree limbs and leaves. 
American pioneers built their tents almost exclusively of hides and canvas with strong 
cordage and sturdy frames. If you are looking to build a long shelter do it the way the 
pioneers did and not the way a survivalist on television might tell you to. 
Hidden Prefab 
Next, we come to the hidden prefab shelter which is what many preppers refer to as the 
bunker. These range in sizes and shapes and are most dependent on your ability to pay 
for the building and installation of such a shelter. These shelters seem to be the go to 
method for preppers with deeper pockets. 
The idea is that when all hell breaks loose up above you and your loved ones can shimmy 
on down below into your bunker. You will have this thing stocked with food, water, clean 
air and as many amenities as you can fit and afford. Here you wait out the ugliness above. 
These prefabs can be effective but I have always been leery about throwing a family of 
four together in close quarters for a month or longer. I don't like the outcomes. Also, there 
is a bit of pride that goes into scurrying underground as well. Of course, if you have no 
other options then hiding out is not the worst thing that could happen to you. 
If you choose to add a prefabbed shelter to your EMP self -sufficiency plan then shop 
around and be very thoughtful about how you will live in your shelter.

2. 2 Liter Bottle Fishing 
This is another method of catching fish in a survival situation. It is most often done using 
2-liter bottles but depending on the fish you are after you could even use regular 12 oz. 
soda bottles.  The  bottles must be  fully intact and have a lid or you m ust be able to use 
duct tape or something to make them airtight. 
To these airtight bottles you will tie some line and hook to  the  lip  below  the screw top. 
Add your bait which could range from worms to food scraps. You will also tie a second 
line to these bottles that will be left on shore. I prefer to anchor these to the shoreline by 
tying them to a stick or to a large rock. 
You are effectively creating a large bobber with a line and baited hook attached to it. The 
second line that is left onshore will be how you retrieve your rig later in the day. The best 
part about this setup is you will see the bottles bouncing up and down  when you have a 
fish on the hook. 
Another great benefit to this rig is having the ability to toss  several  of  these bottles into 
the water and hook them  to  the  shore  to  be  left.  You  can  leave these bottles afloat in 
a pond or slow-moving creek all day while you are out foraging or hunting for game. When 
you put multiple methods to work on food procurement you are taking advantage of self-
sufficiency. 
3. Fish Trap 
An ancient stone fish trap was found in Alaska dating as far back as 500 years. This is a 
viable method for catching fish that has been in use by humans all over the world. Some 
hunter gatherer groups still use them today.  
There are many ways to create these traps but we are going to focus on the method that 
utilizes sticks in shallow water.

62 
Chapter 18 - Security Hacks After an EMP 
When the power grid is fried you will lose most of your security measures in your home.  
Your alarm system will be offline as will the services that it would contact in the event of 
a break in. If you utilize cameras for security measures they will also be inoperable. How 
you present your home will be everything in this situation. 
The good news is you will not be gone from your home very often, if at all. This means that 
you will not  have  to  concern  yourself  with  an  empty  home.  Still, you will want to 
bolster security as there will be  desperate  people  doing desperate things. Whether they 
know you are storing resources or not they may want to come in and look. 
Lock Improvements 
Many average thieves know how to bump an average lock. They can use a special key to 
get into your home by this technique called bumping. Upgraded locks and the addition of 
deadbolts will make this much harder for those looking to get in and cause havoc. 
Outfit all your doors with the upgraded locks and be sure they are secure always. Even 
during the day when someone could just wander into a quiet home. There will be no 
doctors and a fight is the last thing you want to get involved with. 
Sliding Glass Doors 
If your home features these sliding glass doors you will want to make some decisions on 
those. The lock mechanisms on these are pitiful not to mentioned they are on large rock 
away from being shattered providing free entrance into your home. 
One option with glass doors is to seal them off from the outside. You can use scrap wood 
or metal that will cover them up from the outside and you will no longer have to concern 
yourself with them. 
Following an EMP glass doors will be too much of a liability. They are just too easy to get 
into.

Chapter 19 - What You Will Miss Most 
When the lights go out for good you will be forced into a self-reliant lifestyle. In an instant, 
many of the things that make your life what it is will go away. There will be no weaning 
period for these things they will simply cease to exist. In this trans ition, you will face a 
serious longing for the way things used to be 
Some things you will miss more than others. While not having a mailbox full of bills might 
feel pretty good but never receiving another package from Amazon might not. In fact, the 
idea that there is no Amazon period might scare you to death. 
Let's have a look at some of the things you will miss most following an EMP strike. 
Sometimes being prepared is about understanding what you will lose. The mental 
preparation can be invaluable. 
Convenience 
We live an incredibly easy life of convenience. Even those who are bad off in our society 
are still living at a level of convenience that is unparalleled in history. Our access to 
processed resources is nearly unlimited for the average person. After an EMP you will no 
longer have access to the things you want, instantaneously. In fact, you will have to make 
or trade for the things you want and need. 
Light 
Walking into a room and hitting a switch goes away as well. The power of light bathing 
those dark corners and hidden areas only becomes possible by  candle light. Of course, 
you can only have candles if you learn  how  to make them  or barter for them. 
Candles can be made relatively easily if you have access to wax of some sort. This could 
be something you get from your bees. We will discuss bees later in this book. 
Security 
I do not only mean the idea  of  electronic  security  systems  but  I  am  talking about the 
feeling of security. In this new world that follows and EMP people will be very different.

There will be those who adapt and become self -sufficient and there will be those who 
want to take from others. 
Though your property may be well protected and far from many threats you will never 
achieve the security of a civil society. The early days of the EMP will be much worse. Still, 
you will never lay your head on the pillow and feel the way you did before the EMP 
World Wide Connection 
At a time when you want to know  the  condition  of  things  all  over  the  world your power 
to do so will be taken away. Your phones will be inoperable as will your WIFI and internet 
connection. Being  able  to  learn  about  the  events  in Mosul over a coffee in the morning 
will disappear overnight. 
There will be no answers to the issues in your area let alone those  on  a national level. 
You will have to attempt to discern between what's real and what's gossip. The constant 
reminder that you once could see all and now you are limited to only that whi ch stands 
before you. 
Temperature Modification 
What's better than coming in from the snow into a nice warm home? A nice warm home 
that is heated by natural gas and not the strain and stress of seasoned wood will become 
a thing of the past. Heating your home will be possible but it will take some time and effort 
that you aren't used to investing. You may also need to buy a wood stove as well. 
Cooling a home in the heat of summer becomes much more difficult without Freon and 
air conditioning. You will not be able to cool the home even remotely close to what was 
capable with the good old AC. You will miss this most on those 88 -degree nights when 
sleep becomes a sweaty hassle. 
New Stuff 
Becoming self-sufficient after an EMP will depend on you. One part of that change is the 
idea that the only new things you get will be made by you or bartered for with others. These 
items will take some time to be produced. The days of mass production and breakneck 
shipping will be gone. 
This throwaway society that we live in will go away quickly and we will be left to make our 
own

69 
Wet Cooking Methods: 
• Boiling 
• Stewing 
• Poaching 
• Braising 
• Steaming 
There is such freedom in being able to sustain yourself off home cooked meals that are 
delicious. There is no better and more clean method for eating than knowing exactly what 
has gone into your food. 
Processing several types of food is very important to  learn  as  well.  Breaking down meats 
and trimming vegetables are all part of the process of learning to cook from scratch. One 
of the best pieces of advice  is  to  cut  things  in  similar sizes so they will cook evenly. 
One of the most important things to master is creating doughs. Below I  have offered up 
my favorite base  dough  recipe  that  you  can  use  for  many  things. This is a leavened 
dough that rises thanks to the inclusion of yeast. 
Basic Dough Recipe 6 cups of flour 
• 1 cup of lukewarm water 
• 1 packet of dry yeast TBSP of salt 
• Tsp of sugar 
• A few glugs of olive oil 
In a large bowl add your flour and create a nice deep well in the center. Add the water to 
this well along with the sugar and yeast packet. Mix the yeast, water and sugar together 
without pulling in any flour. 
Allow this mix a few minutes to begin to  bubble.  This  will  activate  the yeast and allow it 
to release its dough raising power. 
Next add your salt and a few glugs of olive oil to the well mix. The added fat will make a 
much better dough. 
At this point you want to start incorporating flour into the well gradually. We are not going 
to use all the flour and if you mix it all together you will have a dough that is too stiff. So 
slowly start adding  the  flour  from  the walls of the well into the mix.

use a fork to do this as it helps me be more precise.

the remaining flour to cover your hands and work into the dough. I like to cover with top 
of the dough with flour  and  then  begin folding it on itself while pushing into the center. 
Knead your dough for 8 minutes and then allow it to rest. Cover it will the same bowl you 
mixed it in. I rest the dough for at least 10 minutes. Longer if it's colder in the home. 
At this point you can beat the air out of your dough and form it into anything you like. I use 
this dough to make things like:

72 
The planning of your self-sufficient post EMP garden should look at your entire yard as a 
garden. Utilize your shady areas to grow things like lettuces that do not require as much 
sun. Once you have decided which areas are getting the most sun now you can break up 
your yard into sections and start assigning plants. 
Take advantage of companion planting. In other words, plant vegetables together that 
have a symbiotic relationship that will help them grow and keep away pests. Companion 
planting is a lost method of growing that was used long before synthetic fertilizers and 
pesticides. Here is a look at some of the most popular companion plants: 
• Tomatoes & Cucumbers 
• Potatoes & Cabbage 
• Carrots & Sage 
• Onions & Beets 
• Lettuce & Strawberries 
• Asparagus & Parsley (These are perennials as well) 
Once you have decided where  each  plant  in  your  garden  will  be  placed  you then must 
decide how you are going to grow. You have a few options in this as well. I like to think 
there are three very common ways to grow food. I use these methods and I think there are 
benefits to each: 
• Growing in the Ground 
• Raised Bed Gardening 
• Growing in Pots 
As I said I use all the  methods  listed  above  but I  have  never  had  success  the way I 
have it in raised beds. I am also very partial to growing in pots. Growing food in pots allows 
you to control the sun exposure as well. 
So, it all starts with planning. Spend your time wisely on where and what you plant. Once 
you start breaking ground and  investing  time  and  resources  there are things you cannot 
change. Remember, Lowes will not be open so the seeds of your first crop w ill be very 
important. They may produce the seeds for the rest of your life. 
Water 
The next vital piece of your garden's success is water. How will you water your new garden 
without the water flowing in the pipes around you? After an EMP you will not have safe 
water if any water coming out of the hose.

The best bet will be digging a well just like we mentioned in the earlier chapter on water. 
A well can provide water for your garden at all times and the amount is more than enough 
to water all your plants. 
You will want to include as much water collection into your gardening plan as possible. 
When you are planning water collection you will need a  gallon  per person per day 
minimum and depending on your  garden  size  you  will  need water for that as well. 
An unfiltered local creek can also provide expansive water for your garden. As a young 
man, my father would bring home buckets of water from the creek we fished along with 
the fish inside the buckets. We would clean and eat the fish and the scraps and wate r 
went into the garden.

An Army Engineer’s Emp-Proof Home Guide 
74 
Chapter 22 – Composting 
There is a way to feed your garden each and every year off just what's around your home. 
The miracle of decomposition creates nitrogen which  feeds  your plants in a big  way.  
This is  no new process  and  it  was  even put to  use by  some of America’s founding 
fathers. George Washington  was  a  proponent  of composting as well. 
Below there is a very interesting recipe for settlers’ compost: 
On the North American continent, the benefits of compost were enjoyed by both native 
Americans and early European settlers of America. Many New England farmers made 
compost as a recipe of 10 parts muck to 1 part fish, periodically turning their compost 
heaps until the fish disintegrated (except the bones).  
Today we have found ways to hasten the process and many of us have removed protein 
from our compost piles altogether. Most of us are using leaves, grass clippings and food 
scraps. What we are looking to achieve is a 30:1 ratio of Carbon to Nitrogen. 
Your leaves and yard waste like small twigs are great sources of carbon. Meanwhile your 
green grass clippings are excellent sources of nitrogen. 
The beauty of a compost pile is that it can merely be a pile. It doesn’t need to be anything 
fancy. Some people have tumblers that they fill with compost to be turned. Other people 
have boxes. If you are new to composting get some used pallets for free and use them to 
create a two to three  bin  set  where  you  can throw your compost piles. 
There are many things that you can do to hasten the process of your compost breakdown. 
Turning 
Aeration is huge when it comes to composting. The more you turn your pile the more 
oxygen you are giving the microorganisms in that pile. They are going to eat that stuff up 
and work harder to break your pile down.

75 
Adding 
Many composters swear by a mix of beer and ammonia that kickstarts the breakdown 
process. It also invites worms up from the  ground  to  feast  on  the easy sugars in the 
beer. They, in turn, aid in the breaking down process. This mix is placed in a hose s pray 
bottle and sprayed a couple times a week. 
Covering 
Using a simple tarp to cover your compost pile will keep it from drying out. The moisture 
will feed your little microbiology farm inside your compost pile. The sun's harmful UV rays 
can damage your decomposition troops as well. So, keep them protected with a tarp. 
In your garden, you are growing food but in your compost pile you are growing an army of 
microbiology that work fast to eat up what you put into your pile. Take care of your worms 
and your micros and they will feed the food that feeds you.

Chapter 23 - Building Without Power 
The struggle with self -sufficient building without power is the processing of raw 
ingredients. In other words, it's less about the hammering and nailing and more about 
turning an oak tree into 2X4s.  
Remember those powerful saws and machines that handle this work will be offline 
thanks to the debilitating EMP strike. 
Milling lumber and  cutting steel will require a great deal of  energy and maybe even some 
animal power to achieve the results you are looking for. A good collection of non-powered 
hand tools is a great starting point for this. 
All success in building comes down to having the right tools for the job. Of the many 
failures, I have had in building and home improvement they can almost always be linked 
back to my unwillingness to invest in the right tool.  
In most cases you will try to sub a tool for what you really need and this will tack hours 
onto a job. While the big box hardware stores are open make sure you have the things you 
need.

An Army Engineer’s Emp-Proof Home Guide 
84 
Chapter 26 - Amish Preservation Methods 
In the United States, there are few societies of people who are as self -sufficient as the 
Amish. Though they live a lifestyle that very few envy, this day and age, they have 
mastered their way of life. There is much that we can learn from these people who have 
basically been off grid homesteading since they were able. 
The first settlements were around Lancaster County, Pennsylvania as far back as the 
early 1700’s. They have been perfecting their craft for almost 300 years and bring a wealth 
of knowledge on how to make the most of the land around you. 
One of the cornerstones of the homestead is a vast array  of  preserved  foods. These 
foods are preserved both to take advantage of a large harvest that would otherwise expire 
before being able to be eaten as well as  saving  food  for  the harsh winter to  come. Your  
actions  on  the  homestead  or  in  a  self-sufficient, post EMP scenario will be very similar. 
Sorghum 
This tall flowering grass has been used by the Amish for a long, long time to create one of 
the ultimate survival foods known as sweet sorghum.  This product is like a molasses and 
is derived from the mature grass. You will derive the juice from the whole shoots once the 
plumage of seeds begins to appear. 
This grass is extremely hardy and will survive when many crops will not. That is what 
makes this such a great crop to grow and preserve. The sweet sorghum can be used in all 
the ways a dark, sticky molasses can but it has a better nutritional profile. 
The basic ration is 8:1 i.e. for every 8 gallons of sorghum juice you will yield one gallon 
boiled down. 
Canned Foods 
Canning food has gained some traction in  popularity  and  the  Amish  have  it down to a 
science. The  process  of  canning  is  not  very  difficult.   
You  may struggle with processing all the product you are  planning  to  can.  This  can  be 
time consuming but once you have those jars sanitized  and  filled  you  are basically 
following a recipe.

Something like a ham or, even better, a country ham will store for months at a time due to

87 
Chapter 27 - Managing Livestock 
About the least effective method of attaining a self-sufficient source of meat protein is by 
hunting. If you plan on eating meat on a regular basis don't count on hunting. It's just very 
hard and when you have swaths of other people hunting as well it will only get harder. 
Depending on where you live when the EMP strikes you may be limited in what types of 
livestock you can keep on your property. If you are in the city limits you may not be able 
to keep any livestock at all. 
You can change the  rules on livestock in  your  locality. It will take time and you will have 
to come before city council but it can  be  changed.  The  bigger  your group and the louder  
your  cause  the  better  the  chances.  These  are  steps  to take now so you are prepared 
for tomorrow. 
After an EMP you will be left  with  a  strange  and  almost  opposite  dilemma.  If you 
couldn’t keep livestock in your locality you probably had access to  the livestock but were 
restricted in your ability to keep them.  
After an EMP the last concern of the governing bodies will be whether or not you have 
some chickens clucking around. Of course, you will struggle to find people who have 
livestock to offer if you are in a more rural area. 
Meat 
Your best source of self-sufficient meat is going to be raising livestock on your property. 
Of course, property size and quality is going to dictate how much and what type of 
livestock you can raise. The two best sources of meat for smaller properties are going to 
be chickens and rabbits. 
Both animals will require minimal room with maximum access to eat. If you are smart you 
will maintain a large laying contingent and as those hens stop laying they can be eaten. 
Eating older meat is never going to be as good as tender young animals but it w ill keep 
your eggs laying and your meat source available. 
Rabbits are incredibly prolific they will produce and produce and produce. This makes 
them such an ideal animal for  meat production.  Their droppings are also great for the 
garden. No need to compost them like a chicken’s

90 
• Substitute Sugar 
Keeping bees will require some research. There are three very important things that you 
will need if you are going to plan to keep bees on your property. They can be very 
dangerous if you do not manage them properly. 
Water 
Bees need water and they will need access primarily  in  the  spring.  You  must have a 
body of water or water source nearby so that they can get the water they need. You want 
to keep your bees local as they will do you no  good  if  they abandon your hive and create 
another in a more favorable location. 
Fence 
Having a clear barrier between your bees and your family is crucial. If you have children, 
pets or people who are allergic to bees  than  this  is  even  more important. The  
segregation of these bees will also allow them to have their own space where they feel 
safe. This will help with the quality of the hive and production of honey. 
Smoke 
Smoke is the number one way to get the bees under control. If you plan to manage a hive 
you will need to learn how to employ smoke.

Chapter 29 – Permaculture 
Permaculture is not backyard gardening. Now, you can modify your backyard garden 
using permaculture principles. Permaculture is a harmonious system of growing that 
involves 6 very specific types of plants to work hand in hand with one another.  
The best systems employ as many perennial plants as possible to make a sustainable 
system. 
There is also a great emphasis on the protection of soil. Permaculture puts a lot of weight 
on helping soil along by protecting it from UV rays and flooding.  
These systems are almost always planted directly into the ground and do not benefit from 
the perfect soils of a raised bed. 
Your permaculture system will require quite a bit of planning and will include the following 
types of plants: 
• Canopy (large fruit and nut trees that offer some shade and protection) 
• Dwarf Tree (these smaller trees will produce more food and help shade out weeds) 
• Shrubs (these will be your berry producers) 
• Herbaceous (whether you choose medicinal herbs or culinary they will be in this 
section) 
• Rhizosphere (these will be root crops like carrots, sweet potatoes or turnips)

Most permaculture layouts will follow a pattern of concentric circles starting with the 
large canopy and surrounding it with items 2 - 6 leaving the climbers just for under the 
trees. 
Water collection is another important part of permaculture. With such importance put on 
the soil the idea is to water your plants only with rainwater.  
Our tap water contains levels of chlorine amongst other things that will destroy the 
microbiology in your soil. Water collection will already be a part of your plan but this is yet 
another use for that water. 
You want a system that will work for you year over year. Unlike tilling the earth each year 
and starting from scratch you want to plant perennials that return and require minimal  
time and effort on your end. This is all possible and is being done on properties and in 
communities all over the world. 
Camouflaged Survival Garden 
Another benefit of the post EMP permaculture food source is the look. When you think 
about the traditional garden it stands out in a regular back yard of green grass. Between 
the raised beds and the spaced plants, it's all very unnatural looking.  
In a desperate post EMP situation people are going to eat your garden when you aren't 
looking. Rabbits will be the least of your worries. 
The beauty of a permaculture system is that it all grows together. It all runs together and 
becomes a beautiful mess. Sometimes it tangles and the climbers get out of control. 
From a distance, the average person will not know they are looking at a food source. 
This process is taking companion planting to the next level. Its designed to work with and 
make the most of your land. Though the backyard garden is a perfect way to start growing 
food you will want to consider permaculture for true self sufficiency. 
The day may come when we see the sky light up and the lights go out. It could be from 
war, it could be from the sun or it could be from some force deep in space that we are 
unaware of.
